image_description: A museum display featuring a fossilized Triceratops skeleton mounted in a walking pose. The skeleton is dark grey/black, set against a light beige sandy floor and a background of glass cases and informational signage. The skull features the characteristic three horns and large frill. The limbs are columnar with visible digit claws.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount clearly displays two large supraorbital horns and one smaller nasal horn, matching the anatomical description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a fossilized skeleton (bone). The 'keratinous cutting edge' refers to soft tissue (beak sheath) which is not preserved or present in this skeletal mount. Only the bony rostral core is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeleton stands on four sturdy, vertical limbs consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large parietal-squamosal frill is clearly visible behind the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as solid bone structure typical of a fossil cast/skeleton.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a bare skeleton; no skin, scales, or soft tissue impressions are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertebral column slopes downward from hips to shoulders, consistent with shorter forelimbs.
The tail vertebrae are visible and appear relatively short compared to other dinosaur types.

The connection between the lower leg bones and the foot digits is blurry and indistinct, suggesting poor definition or potential AI generation artifact in the skeletal joints.
Text on the background signs is illegible and warped, typical of AI-generated backgrounds or depth-of-field blur issues.
